reviews.body:
Reproduced #2627 on main with a backend stress test on Linux: 23/1510 GETs had an ETag that wasn't MD5(body), and every If-Match hit in that window returned the wrong body. With this PR the xattr GET case drops to 0. Thanks! Before merge:
1. CI: `TestGetObjectRemovedBeforeOpen` fails (inline).
2. HeadObject has the same split (stat, then ETag by path): 309/4500 HEADs returned a ContentLength from a different version than the ETag. HEAD followed by ranged GETs with If-Match is a common client pattern. Please fix it here or open a follow-up.
3. Sidecar is unchanged (~13% of GETs mismatched under the same load). `Fixes #2627` will close the issue, so please open a follow-up for sidecar/HEAD, or note in the issue that this fix is xattr-only.

review_comments.body: This breaks `TestGetObjectRemovedBeforeOpen/versioned_directory_replaced_by_object` (fails on Linux and macOS). The open now runs before `liveObjVersionId`, so by the time `getAttrTags(bucket, object, versionId)` runs, `versionId` holds the live version's id. A versioned GET with no versionId that races a delete now returns `NoSuchVersion` instead of `NoSuchKey`. Commit 1 had this right with `getString(input.VersionId)`; 207a4b41 reverted it. Please restore it, or read the tags from `f`. The description says `go test ./backend/posix` passes, but it doesn't at HEAD.

The ETag now comes from `f`, but `x-amz-version-id` still comes from a path read in `liveObjVersionId` (L6291, and L6258 for the 304), and that read now happens *after* the open. In a 3-writer/3-reader stress test on a versioned bucket, GETs whose VersionId didn't match the returned body went from 6–16/1800 on main to 20–42/1800 with this PR. Reading `versionIdKey` from `f` (e.g. pass `f` into `liveObjVersionId`) brought it to 0.

Same root cause, still open: when `versionId` names the live version, L6124 resolves it by path, and this open can land on a newer version that a concurrent PUT just linked. About 2% of `GET ?versionId=` reads during an overwrite return another version's body. With this PR that body also gets its own ETag, while `VersionId` still names the requested version. If the request resolved to the live path, check `versionIdKey` on `f` after the open and reopen from the versioning dir if it differs (0 mismatches with that change).

`TestGetObjectRemovedBeforeOpen` no longer reaches this branch. Its trigger reads (`etagkey` / `versionIdKey`) now happen after the open, so its "removed" cases pass through `getAttrTags` instead. Coverage shows 0 hits here on this PR, 1 on main. Please update the test so the object is still removed between the stat and this open; otherwise the ENOTDIR/ESTALE → NoSuchKey mapping from be69ca6f is untested.

With the fd read, any error (ESTALE on a shared FS, EIO, ...) silently becomes `p.defaultEtag`. That made-up ETag then decides If-Match/If-None-Match and is returned as the object's ETag, which is the kind of bug this PR fixes. Please fall back only on `meta.ErrNoSuchKey` and return other errors.

The 304 path still reads the parts count (and tags) by path in `notModifiedCounts` (L6263), while the 200 path now reads `mpMetaKey` from `f` (L6374), so a 304 can report another version's `PartsCount`. Pass `f` through for the mp metadata read.

`f.Stat()` on an open fd can't return ENOENT/ENOTDIR/ENAMETOOLONG, so these mappings are dead code. The ENOENT case also returns `InvalidArgument`, while the open above maps the same condition to `NoSuchVersion`. Since the block is moving anyway, reduce it to `if err != nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("stat object: %w", err) }`.
Nit: the open now runs before `liveObjVersionId`, so `versionId` is still the requested one here. Use `versionId`, as L6229 does, instead of `getString(input.VersionId)`.

Nit: swapping the `closeFile` closure (here, L6224, L6456) is harder to follow than a flag, e.g. `defer func() { if f != nil && !bodyOwned { f.Close() } }()` with `bodyOwned = true` after `buildGetObjectBody`. Note that this defer also fixes fd leaks on main's error returns after the open (416, InvalidPartNumber, tag/checksum errors); worth a line in the description.

Nit: this comment is long and describes PutObject and XattrMeta internals. Two lines are enough: "Open before reading attributes so the ETag, preconditions and body come from one inode. Directory objects have no data file and stay path-based."

This only checks that the ETag is read through `f`. The PR also moved the mtime, the 304 metadata and the part map to `f`, and none of those are covered. Consider making the fake diverge for `mpMetaKey` too (a `partNumber` GET) and adding an `If-None-Match` → 304 case. Also, "is the window a GET has" reads oddly; describe what the fake returns.
Nit: avoid `'` in subtest names; it makes `-run` patterns awkward.

Please also add an integration test. The unit test above only checks that the ETag is read through `f`; a race test checks the S3 behavior end to end and catches any later change that moves a read back to the path. `HeadObject_GetObject_race_with_delete` in `tests/integration/posix.go` is a good model.

Suggested shape: 4 writers PUT unique bodies to one key while 4 readers GET it (every other GET with `If-Match` of the previous ETag). Record ETag → MD5(body) from the PUT responses. After the run, check that each GET's body is the one put with its ETag, and that each If-Match 200 returned that ETag's body. Don't assume ETag == MD5, so it also works with `--data-integrity-etag`.

I ran a draft of this against a real gateway: it failed 10/10 runs on main and passed 8/8 on this branch. A correct gateway can't fail it, so it isn't flaky.

Catch: `runtests.sh --sidecar` runs the `posix` group against a sidecar gateway without a sidecar flag, and sidecar still fails this test (~30% of reads). Either add a `--sidecar` flag to the `posix` test subcommand and skip the test with it, or fix sidecar here too. If you fix the VersionId read (comment above), a versioned variant that also checks `VersionId` would cover that.

Small gap in the new reopen path: it doesn't re-check for a delete marker. If `versionId` names the live delete marker and a PUT moves it to the versioning dir between the version-id lookup and the `isObjDeleteMarker` check, that check sees the new object and this reopens the marker's file. The GET then returns 200 with the body and ETag of the version the marker hides (markers are made in place and keep its data), instead of 405 MethodNotAllowed with `x-amz-delete-marker: true`. Reproduced deterministically with `beforeReadMeta` on `deleteMarkerKey`. main is also wrong here (it returns the new object's body), so not a regression, but a perfect spot to fix it. Read `deleteMarkerKey` from the reopened `f` and return the same delete-marker response as the check above.

Nit: the 304 path now also reads Cache-Control/Expires/metadata and the lock settings from `f`, but nothing covers it: switching that `loadObjectMetaProperties` call back to `nil` keeps every test green. A stale path value for one of those attributes, checked in this subtest, would cover it.
Nit: this doc comment still describes the old trigger (the live version-id lookup), and the new `directory object removed` case is never opened. Worth a refresh.

Nit: `bucket != origBucket` is also true when the version was in the versioning dir from the start, where the path check above already ran, so this adds a delete-marker read to every GET of a non-current version. A `reopened` flag set in the reopen block would limit it to the case it's for. Also, an `IsEntryGone` error here returns a 500, while the ETag read below maps the same error to `goneErr()`.
Nit: every other test in this file has a doc comment; one line describing the interleaving (the marker is moved to the versioning dir between the lookup and the delete-marker check) would match.

comments.body: This won't automatically run in continuous integration without approval. A member of the Versity organization must allow it.

Thanks for the detailed review. The new commits on top address it:

- **CI / `TestGetObjectRemovedBeforeOpen`**: tags are looked up with the requested version id again, so a versioned GET with no `versionId` that races a delete answers `NoSuchKey`. `go test ./backend/posix` passes at this HEAD.
- **`x-amz-version-id`**: `liveObjVersionId` now takes `f`, for the 200 and the 304. `TestGetObjectLiveVersionIdFromOpenedFile` replaces the object after the open; reading the id by path turns it red.
- **`?versionId=` naming the live version**: the id on the opened inode is checked, and the version is reopened from the versioning dir if a PUT moved it.
- **Removed object test**: `TestGetObjectRemovedBeforeOpen` reaches the open branch again. It also covers a removed directory object.
- **ETag read errors**: only a missing attribute falls back to the default ETag; anything else fails the GET.
- **304**: the parts count now comes from `f`. The fake store diverges for `mpMetaKey` too, with a `partNumber` GET and a 304 case.
- **Nits**: the `f.Stat()` mappings are gone, the open uses the requested version id, `closeFile` became a `bodyOwned` flag, the comment is two lines, and the subtest names have no `'`. That flag also fixes the fd leaks on main's error returns after the open.
- **Integration test**: `GetObject_etag_race_with_put` follows your shape: 4 writers and 4 readers on one key, with ETag -> body recorded from the PUT responses and no ETag == MD5 assumption. With main's `posix.go` it failed 2/2. On this branch the `posix` suite passed 3/3 plain, 3/3 with `-vs` and 2/2 with `--data-integrity-etag`.
- **Sidecar**: added `--sidecar-test-mode` to the `posix` test subcommand, and `runtests.sh` passes it on the four `posix` runs, so the test is skipped there (2/2 on a `--sidecar` gateway). `runtests.ps1` already gets it through `--windows-test-mode`.
- **Scope**: this fixes the xattr GET only. HEAD and sidecar are not changed here, and #2627 now has a note saying so, with the numbers you measured. I can take HEAD next if you want it.

The versioned variant of the race test that also checks `VersionId` is not included; the unit test above covers that read.

(Reply drafted with the help of an AI coding assistant.)

The reopened version now checks deleteMarkerKey through f and returns the existing delete-marker response. TestGetObjectDeleteMarkerMovedAfterLookup reproduces the reported interleaving and fails before the fix. The 304 subtest now checks Cache-Control with a stale path value; changing its loadObjectMetaProperties call back to nil fails that assertion. The removal-test comment now describes the delete-marker read trigger and the directory-object case. The full posix unit suite passes.

This comment was drafted with Claude Code.
